turns.text: I was looking at my card statement this morning, and there is this unfamiliar line that keeps popping up over and over. Can you track down what it is actually for?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
I can see the October statement on your Personal Visa (5501). There are eight line items, and one that stands out as possibly unfamiliar — but let me lay out both candidates:

**Fenwick Lang & Co. — $29.00 on October 21.** That's the same company that sent the private placement pitch (Meridian Yield Opportunity II). $29.00 is far too small to be the $25,000 subscription, but it could be a fee, a book, or an information pack they charged for. Do you remember authorising that?

**Glenmont Card Services — $385.00 on October 26.** This one is the card issuer itself charging the card. It could be a payment you set up (like autopay from the card to itself), a service fee, a credit product, or something else. It falls on the period close date, which is typical for recurring charges.

The November statement has not been issued yet — the period closes on the 26th of each month, so it should land any day now. If this charge you are seeing repeats across both statements, the "Glenmont Card Services" line is the most likely recurring candidate.

Do either of those ring a bell? If you can describe the unfamiliar line — roughly how much and what vendor name you are seeing — I can pin it down further.

| Charge | Amount | Date | What I found |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fenwick Lang & Co.** | $29.00 | Oct 21 | The contact record says this firm "sends the same pitch every few weeks." You already received another pitch from them on November 3. If the $29 repeats at the same cadence as the pitches, that fits "over and over." |
| **Glenmont Card Services** | $385.00 | Oct 26 | Charged on the period close date by the card issuer to its own card. That pattern — same amount, same vendor, same day of the period — is the textbook shape of a recurring monthly charge. |

The November statement (available online, not as a bill document I can read) would show which of these two appears again on it — and I would bet one of them does.

Can you describe more about the line you are seeing? The vendor name, the amount, or how often it hits — even roughly? That will pin it down to one of these two straight away.
